java_locations.role: Recognizes bracketed link-style clauses within the shaft, maps `hidden` into an invisible LinkType, and still creates and adds the Link event.
Keeps invisible links in the diagram/layout collection but excludes them from the semantic single-visible-link count used for preliminary Opale eligibility.
Serializes the invisible edge to Graphviz so it constrains routing, then suppresses its ordinary SVG paint group.
Exposes invisibility as link semantics independently from link existence, source order and UID.

rust_locations.role: The shaft scanner rejects `[` before a complete arrow is parsed, so a valid `-[hidden]-` command vanishes instead of producing a connection.
Has no semantic visibility channel, preventing layout and paint from treating one retained relation differently.
All retained connections already participate in layout and UID order, but every connection is counted for Opale incidence and painted because visibility is absent.

claimed_invariant: A valid Deployment `hidden` bracket style creates one explicit invisible DeploymentConnection at the command source line. It retains cleaned endpoints, direction, labels, shaft length and source-order link UID exactly like a visible relation. The edge participates in Graphviz layout and can change other solved routes, but emits no ordinary SVG link group, path, arrowhead or label. Invisible incident links are excluded from GraphvizImageBuilder's preliminary one-visible-link count for a named note; their layout effect can still make the remaining visible edge multi-cubic and revoke Opale later.
causal_divergence: Rust treated the arrow shaft as a flat character run and had no link visibility field. Encountering the Java bracket style terminates scanning, so the whole command falls through and disappears. That erases an event rather than making it invisible, changing topology, layout constraints, Opale routing and every later global UID.
planned_model_change: Extend Deployment arrow scanning to retain bracket style clauses while deriving arrowhead, direction, line style and length from the bracket-free shaft. Capture whether any style token is `hidden` and store it on DeploymentConnection. Add every hidden edge to layout and UID allocation as today, exclude it from visible Opale incidence, and skip only its SVG paint phase. Preserve labels and endpoint metadata in the AST even though paint is suppressed.

acceptance: The rejecting visible-plus-hidden probe retains two AST connections and assigns AfterHidden ent0007 while painting no hidden link group.
The hidden edge participates in layout sufficiently for the visible edge's solved-cubic Opale decision to match Java.
A lone hidden note link is ignored by the preliminary visible-incidence count but still consumes its link UID.
Ordinary hidden node-to-node links constrain layout, consume UIDs and paint nothing.
An independent checker attacks style slot, direction, endpoint side, labels, layout direction, incidence and downstream UID order.

painting the edge and deleting its SVG group post hoc
counting invisible links as visible Opale incidence

declared_residue: Other bracket styles such as norank, thickness, color and compound style lists remain separate style semantics, though the scanner must not misparse them as endpoint text.
Unsupported endpoint notation forms remain separate.
Generic Graphviz route-coordinate differences remain a layout mechanism.
